item.title: Meta Reinforcement Learning
item.description: In my earlier post on meta-learning , the problem is mainly defined in the context of few-shot classification. Here I would like to explore more into cases when we try to “meta-learn” Reinforcement Learning (RL) tasks by developing an agent that can solve unseen tasks fast and efficiently. To recap, a good meta-learning model is expected to generalize to new tasks or new environments that have never been encountered during training. item.title: Domain Randomization for Sim2Real Transfer
item.description: In Robotics, one of the hardest problems is how to make your model transfer to the real world. Due to the sample inefficiency of deep RL algorithms and the cost of data collection on real robots, we often need to train models in a simulator which theoretically provides an infinite amount of data. However, the reality gap between the simulator and the physical world often leads to failure when working with physical robots. item.title: Meta-Learning: Learning to Learn Fast
